products.description: Geometric Ginza Stone Tin-on-Tin Cocktail Shaker Be part of the first chapter in an exciting collaboration between Urban Bar and InkedOz with this exclusive Geometric Ginza Tin-on-Tin Cocktail Shaker, available only through the Urban Bar website. Created in partnership with Daniel “Oz” Osborne — known for sharing his bartending expertise online, leading training within hospitality, and championing both professional development and well-being in the industry — this special release celebrates craftsmanship, performance, and the culture of modern bartending. Made from premium 18/8 Japanese steel, the Ginza Tin-on-Tin Cocktail Shaker set includes our Ginza Can and Ginza Cup. Its high-grade steel construction delivers a lighter, more robust finish than standard barware, while offering superior insulation for a colder, more effective shake. Favoured by professional mixologists, it also produces a satisfying rattle as the ice moves through the full steel body, adding a touch of theatre to every serve. A silver-welded base provides added strength, while the steel’s excellent corrosion resistance helps protect against rust for lasting durability. As the very first Urban Bar x InkedOz release, this is an exclusive collaboration piece designed for bartenders who take their craft seriously. Product Features: Professional dual shaker tin set Made from premium 18/8 Japanese steel for greater corrosion resistance Outlasts standard poor grade steel shakers Unique Tumbled Stone Finish Both tins are weighted on the base

products.title: Doorly's 14 Year Old- 70cl
products.description: Single Blended Rum Made predominantly in countries that were colonised by the British, Single Blended Rums are blends that have been distilled in both pot and traditional column stills used for making rum. The two types of rums are then blended at a Single distillery. The Foursquare Distillery that creates Doorlys Rum has been voted the best rum distillers in the world for the past 3 years. They take pride in the fact that all their rums are natural and unadulterated. This tasty rum is blended then aged for a minimum of 14 years in once used Bourbon whiskey barrels. Serving Suggestions: Perfect neat or on the rocks with a twist of orange or lime peel. If cocktails are your thing then try this rum in a Manhattan styled drink with 2 parts Doorlys, 1-part sweet vermouth and a couple of dashes of bitters. Tasting Notes On the nose youll find deep aromas of exotic fruits and sweet toffee with a bright ginger note. The palate is rich and layered with vanilla, a bit of almonds, orange zest, and cooked berries. The finish is nicely long with cinnamon, toasted wood and a touch of cacao.
products.descriptionHtml:
Single Blended Rum

Made predominantly in countries that were colonised by the British, Single Blended Rums are blends that have been distilled in both pot and traditional column stills used for making rum. The two types of rums are then blended at a Single distillery.

The Foursquare Distillery that creates Doorlys Rum has been voted the best rum distillers in the world for the past 3 years. They take pride in the fact that all their rums are natural and unadulterated. This tasty rum is blended then aged for a minimum of 14 years in once used Bourbon whiskey barrels.

Serving Suggestions: Perfect neat or on the rocks with a twist of orange or lime peel. If cocktails are your thing then try this rum in a Manhattan styled drink with 2 parts Doorlys, 1-part sweet vermouth and a couple of dashes of bitters.

Tasting Notes

On the nose youll find deep aromas of exotic fruits and sweet toffee with a bright ginger note. The palate is rich and layered with vanilla, a bit of almonds, orange zest, and cooked berries. The finish is nicely long with cinnamon, toasted wood and a touch of cacao.

products.title: 1910 Umbo 35cl
products.description: The Umbo 1910 collection reinterprets the Umbo silhouette through a vintage lens. Featuring a delicately etched pattern inspired by early 20th-century glassmaking, each piece combines classic detailing with modern crystalline clarity. The result is a range that feels timeless, elegant and quietly decorative — ideal for refined cocktail service, sparkling drinks and select dessert presentations. The name Umbo, derived from Latin and meaning the rounded centre of a shield, reflects the balanced proportions at the heart of each design, while 1910 references the era that inspired its decorative detailing. The Umbo 1910 35cl combines generous capacity with refined vintage character. Its etched pattern enhances layered and long cocktails, while the crystalline construction ensures clarity and brilliance. Designed to make an impression without overpowering the drink.

Featuring a delicately etched pattern inspired by early 20th-century glassmaking, each piece combines classic detailing with modern crystalline clarity. The result is a range that feels timeless, elegant and quietly decorative — ideal for refined cocktail service, sparkling drinks and select dessert presentations. The name Umbo, derived from Latin and meaning the rounded centre of a shield, reflects the balanced proportions at the heart of each design, while 1910 references the era that inspired its decorative detailing. The Umbo 1910 23cl glass is perfectly suited to short, spirit-forward cocktails. Its delicately etched vintage pattern adds texture and visual depth, while the compact bowl maintains balance and control. Crafted from crystalline for exceptional transparency, it offers a refined nod to classic barware.

products.title: Muddler Bar Spoon 28cm, 2.5ml & 5ml
products.description: The Muddler Bar Spoon was developed with award winning bartender Wayne Collins to give a multi-purpose bar tool. The double sided measuring head lets you measure both 5ml and 2.5ml. The tip is larger and more robust than standard flat end muddlers for far more effective muddling ability. Measure: The spoon is a double-sided measure, approx. 5ml/0.17oz in one side and approx. 2.5ml/0.08oz (a half spoon) in the reverse. It also gives a useful half measure (12.5ml) with 2x 5ml & 1x 2.5ml Perfect for precise mixology. Crushing: The tip of the spoon can be used to crush solid ingredients in the bottom of a glass or cocktail shaker. Stir/Soft Rotation: Push the spoon between thumb and finger to make the spoon head rotate and mix a drink, alternatively plunge with the flat end or simply stir. products.title: Retro Nick & Nora Cocktail Glass 17cl
products.description: With an elegant design, the retro Nick & Nora Glass brings sophistication to any serve. Made from lead-free crystal, this cocktail glass features brilliant transparency to accentuate the contents in a minimal drink presentation. This high level of clarity in the material is paired with an elegantly delicate stem, contrasting with the comparatively large bowl on top. Inspired by vintage 1930s design, this cocktail glass emerged from classic detective film, The Thin Man. Taking its name from the cocktail loving lead characters, Nick & Nora Charles, this crystal stem glass is the perfect embodiment of prohibition era style. Offering a solution to spill-prone wide rimmed martini glasses, the Nick & Nora cocktail glass has tall walls. This reduces the chance of spillage, ensuring the drinker can enjoy the fruits of your mixology. products.title: Yansheng Tin-on-Tin Copper Plated Weighted Shaker 85cl
products.description: This tin on tin shaker is made with a classic Asian shape featuring a premium copper finish giving a slightly heavier, more robust shaker. Made with our standard high level of quality steel and featuring laser welded caps on the base of the two tins. Yansheng Coins are talismans of good fortune in China, and often used to bring in money in Feng Shui. These coins are round with a square hole in the centre. They represent both heaven (the circle) and earth (the square), and because of this, they are deemed especially auspicious. Features Lucky Coins on the base Made from premium 18/8 Japanese steel for greater corrosion resistance Weighted base on each tin for increased rigidity Outlasts standard poor grade steel shakers Polished Copper Plated finish Gift boxed Dishwasher safe - see our Steel Care Guide page for more information

products.title: All Angels Sparkling Rosé 2018- 75cl
products.description: Savour in a moment of tranquility or enjoy in good company with canapés; this versatile rosé, reminiscent of sunny summer days, is one for all moments that matter. As with any worthy vintage, serve 20 minutes out of the fridge. 2018 is fondly remembered by the vineyards of England as a year when the weather was ideal at all the key times. All Angels had a bountiful harvest of superb quality. With many options to hand, they found the perfect blend for their 2018 Sparkling Rosé, a stunning fruit forward union of Rondo’s rich, red fruit and the tropical influences of Pinot Gris. Serving Suggestions Serve chilled (at around 12C) in Champagne flutes. This pretty pink sparkling wine is ideal as an aperitif but versatile enough to pair nicely with savoury nibbles, quiche lorraine or with afternoon tea. English scones with clotted cream and fresh strawberries pair like a dream. A very English fizz. Tasting Notes A delicate peach colour, with aromas and palate full of nectarine and pomegranate, alongside softly spiced raspberry crumble. Stylishly balanced with a refreshing acidity and fine ascending bubbles.

products.title: The Grange Classic -  75cl
products.description: Complex, rich and layered, this English sparkling wine will give some Champagnes a run for their money. Coming from chalky vineyard slopes in Hampshire facing the River Itchen, just a stones throw from the familys handsome Grange estate (whose Greek Revival architecture graces the label), this is a classic Hampshire Brut made with the holy trinity of Champagne-grapes Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier. With three years aged on its lees in bottle, this takes on a richness and complexity with lingering notes of freshly baked pastry and a creamy, but fresh, finish. One to wow your guests with. Serving Suggestions Serve chilled in a wide-rimmed Champagne flute to let the complex flavours emerge from the glass. This is a classic, richer style of English sparkling wine which will impress guests served with smoked salmon canapés or on its own for a celebration, but can also stand up nicely to creamy lobster or fish dishes at a main meal. If you want to try your hand at sparkling wine cocktails, try this with a dash of fine Cognac (serve the wine into the chilled flute with 25ml cognac). Tasting Notes This wine exudes aromas of crisp, green apples and lemon curd with a toasty undercurrent of aromas of freshly-baked croissants, brioche and apple pie. With a rich, creamy mouthfeel, its a complex wine that lingers but has vibrant acidity that invites you for another sip. And another. And another

products.title: Roebuck Blanc de Noirs 2015 - 75cl
products.description: This handsome Blanc de Noir is a gorgeous drop that will rival many vintage Champagnes. Coming from vineyards near Petworth, this is made from 100% Pinot Noir which has spent almost four years ageing on the lees to result in a wonderfully rich and complex sparkling wine. Roebuck Estate havent been making wines for too long but they are already turning heads with some fabulous awards under their belts, including taking home the prestigious award for Best in Show at Decanter World Wine Awards in 2020. Serving Suggestions Serve chilled in a wide-rimmed sparkling wine glass to allow the richer aromas to emerge. This is a complex wine which suits important celebrations, fine dining or an indulgent night in with a good chunk of aged comté. A wine that will impress and convert Champagne-lovers to the wonderful world of English sparkling wine. Tasting Notes This is a wine that opens and evolves in the glass over time, so take your time lingering over it. Having spent almost four years on the lees it has developed rich aromas of freshly baked croissants and apple pie, with a nutty note of toasted almonds. With fine but mouth-filling bubbles, it lingers for moments with a long, aromatic finish.

products.title: Roebuck Classic Cuvee 2017 -  75cl
products.description: The 2017 growing season started well in the spring with an early budburst followed by dry, sunny weather in May and June and a very early flowering  one of the earliest on record. Fortunately, due to favourable conditions at our West Sussex sites, the vines were protected from the late spring frosts that badly affected Northern Europe vineyards and were able to bask in a long, relatively warm ripening period throughout the summer and autumn months. Picking commenced at the start of October and the fruit benefited from a longer than normal hang time resulting in an excellent quality harvest of perfectly ripe grapes with high sugars and balanced acids. The 2017 growing season will be remembered fondly for its wonderfully elegant sparkling wines with incredible depth of flavour and finesse. Serving Suggestions Serve chilled, around 12 - 14C. This has plenty of complex aromas to enjoy so serve it in a wide-rimmed sparkling wine glass if you can. This is a classic sparkling wine which will work really nicely with canapés, wedding cake, Gougères (French cheese puffs!) or smoked salmon dishes. If you want to play with your sparkling wine cocktails, try it with a dash of fine, old Cognac. Tasting Notes Rich, yet pale lemon in colour. Notes of baked pears and citrus fruits are layered with a toasty richness and hint of sweet spice. Delicate bubbles linger on the palate leading to a long, beautifully balanced finish. This wine is drinking well now but will undoubtedly, continue to improve with additional bottle age.

products.title: Westwell Pelegrim NV  -  75cl
products.description: This crisp, mouthwatering English bubbly is an ode to the pelegrims (or pilgrims as we call them today) that have walked along the Pilgrims Way, which goes right past the vineyard, for several centuries. This classic cuvée is the essence of English sparkling wine: filled with aromas of wild strawberries and crisp green apples. With the classic trio of sparkling wine grapes - Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier - its an inviting, easy-drinking English bubbly from the excellent portfolio of Westwell made by former music producer Adrian Pike. Serving Suggestions Serve well chilled in a sparkling wine flute. This is a bright and refreshing sparkling wine with a pleasing, easy-to-enjoy finish that makes a great aperitivo to be served early in the evening or with weekend brunch. If you fancy trying your hand at a sparkling cocktail with this, take an English spin on the French 75 (a Soixante Quinze ): chill some gin in a cocktail shaker with ice, a splash of syrup and a squeeze of fresh lemon. Strain it into your wine flute, pour over a glass of chilled Westwell Pelegrim and garnish with a lemon peel. Perfect for a party! Tasting Notes Poised and refreshing, this is a very English bubbly with aromas of cider apples, lemon sherbet, spring blossoms and wild strawberries with notes of sourdough bread from three years ageing on the lees.

products.title: Worthy Park Single Estate - 70cl
products.description: Pure Pot Stilled Rum Also known as SINGLE RUMS, these sugarcane spirits are batched distilled in a pot still at a one single distillery. They can be aged or unaged depending on the rules or regulations of the country where the rum is made. The family-run Worthy Park Estate was established in 1670, and started producing rum as early as 1741. An authentic and traditional Jamaican rum and the first release under their Worthy Park range of bottlings. A blend of 100% copper pot-still rums that have been aging between 6-10 years; this blend has been created to showcase the unique complexity and distinctive taste that Worthy Park has to offer. 100% single estate product; batch distilled, aged, blended and bottled on site. Serving Suggestions: This rum is amazing with a splash of premium ginger beer or ale in a rocks glass, large ice cube and a wedge of lime. In a cocktail you should try a Rum old Fashion, with a sugar cube, doused in bitters, then stirred with ice and the rum until cold. Add a twist of orange peel for aroma and garnish. Tasting Notes A natural, light amber color; the nose is punchy with upfront aromas of light tobacco and toasted oak with spicy fruit  raisins and plums. With time light notes of vanilla become evident. On the mouth luscious and tropical fruits with a soft, buttery and almost creamy texture. Dry a slightly bitter, soft tannins are rounded out by toasted oak and nutmeg. A hint of black pepper finished off with a touch of ginger as it lingers with its soft, dry finish.

products.title: Duppy Share Spiced Rum - 70cl
products.description: Spiced Rum In this section we recommend Spiced rums that are a sub category of real rums that have been flavoured with spices through infusion or maceration. Traditionally rums such a there would have been made locally in rum producing countries for medicinal purposes. It has been said that Spiced Rum is the new Gin. A fruity spiced rum from The Duppy Share. The Rum is a blend of young distillate made in Jamaica (Worthy Park and in Barbados (Foursquare). It is then infused with pineapple, kola nut and Caribbean spices to create its unique flavour profile. Serving Suggestions: A must in a tall carbonated drink such as a highball, and a must if your favourite drink is Spiced Rum & ginger beer or ginger ale. If Daiquiris are your thing then try a Spiced Pineapple Daiquiri using fresh lime juice & pineapple infused syrup with a sprinkle of nutmeg as garnish. Tasting Notes On the nose there is an explosion of sweet spicy riped pineapple and kola nuts, the predominant flavours for this spiced rum. On the palate the pineapple and kola nuts continue but slowly make way for ginger, hints of vanilla, cloves and nutmeg. The Duppy spiced is not cloyingly sweet, thus the finishing spiced flavours are not masked by a layer of sugar syrup.

products.title: Equiano - 70cl
products.description: British Premium Rum Historically rums from the ex-British colonies were the most sought after in the world. Today we are seeing a rise in British companies importing rums from around the world to bring world class spirits to the British public under their own brand name. A unique rum that claims to be the worlds first blend of rums from Africa and the Caribbean. The British based company transfer rums aged in ex cognac barrels from Mauritius to Barbados, where it is blended with award winning rums from the Foursquare distillery that have been aged in ex bourbon casks. After resting and bottling, the premium rum is then sent to the UK. The rum is named after 18th century abolitionist and author Olaudah Equiano. Serving Suggestions: Try this rum neat in a warm glass and the oils from a twist of orange. It can also be appreciated in light rum cocktails where it is balanced with citrus and sugar. For a drink with a difference try it in Rum Negroni with a dash of chocolate bitters. Tasting Notes Like any quality premium rum, Equiano subtly delivers tropical warmth as soon as its aroma touches your nose. Rich, notes of dried fruits, raisins & sultanas combine with sweet toffee, butterscotch and caramel culminating with a suggestion of orange peel, vanilla and oak. A warm toffee and butterscotch mouth-feel, with chewy raisins and brown sugar flavours that emerge from the liquid as it caresses your tongue. Equiano is a naturally sweet rum with no added sugar or spices, it has a medium to sweet ending with touches of oak, anise, sweet pepper with a hint of bitter orange peel.

products.title: Copalli White Rum - 70cl
products.description: Light Rum In this section our rums are categorized as light as they are unaged, light in body or lightly aged then filtered through charcoal to remove the colour of the wood. They still retain an incredible amount of aroma, through fermentation, distillation or aging in oak barrels. Copalli Rum is an organic rum made with 100-percent single origin; estate-produced sugarcane that is hand harvested by local workers. Made from the fermented sugarcane juice, Copalli White Rum is a blend of pot and column distilled sugarcane juice. After distillation, its rested on stainless steel for a period of time before being bottled. Serving Suggestions: Try this light rum in a Daiquiri with a sparkling wine float, to add a little freshness garnish with a fresh mint leaf. Or try this Belize white rum with tonic, fresh grapefruit and a touch of agave nectar in a tall glass. Tasting Notes On the nose, Copalli White Rum has a lovely aroma of fresh grass, sugarcane juice, citrus oils and a hint of vanilla. Its flavour is equally bright and fresh. There is a light creaminess on the palate, with a touch of white pepper, herbs, spices and citrus.

products.title: Worthy Park Rum-Bar Silver - 70cl
products.description: Light Rum In this section our rums are categorized as light as they are unaged, light in body or lightly aged then filtered through charcoal to remove the colour of the wood. They still retain an incredible amount of aroma, through fermentation, distillation or aging in oak barrels. Jamaican white rums are known for their pungency, tropical flavours and strength. This rum is no different except a reduced ABV gives it a little more versatility than its stronger counterparts. Made from local molasses, the by-product of local sugarcane, and distilled in a copper pot still, this award-winning molasses rum is a classic Jamaican style. Serving Suggestions: Perfect in rum punches or light cocktails where you want the flavour of the rum to shine through. For a refreshing easy drink why not try a Rise n Shine, which is simple Worthy Park silver & freshly squeezed Orange juice. Tasting Notes A sweet and fragrant un-aged rum, the nose is full of tropical, fruity flavours dominated by banana, pineapple with hints of citrus and vanilla. The aromatic but powerful Jamaican funk will make you feel that this rum is stronger than it really is. But on the palate, it is rich and fruity with buttery, banana notes and candied fruit. The finish is naturally sweet, long with spicy citrus notes and a touch of molasses.

products.title: Diplomatico Reserva Exclusiva - 70cl
products.description: Sweetened Rum Here we recommend rums that have been sweetened with the addition of aged sugar syrup, sweet wines or other sweetening agents to round off the rums flavour. Europe allows a maximum of 20grms of sugar per litre of alcohol to be added to rum. Diplomatico is made at the Destilerias Unidas which is located at the foot of The Andes in the Terepaima National Park. They have been producing top-quality spirits for over 50 years and have achieved cult status with rum lovers across the globe. The distillery was designed for versatility, with three pot stills and four column stills distilling different styles of spirit from top-grade molasses and sugar cane honeys. The rum is a blend of molasses and sugar cane honey, a blend of pot and column still rum that has been aged from 2 to 12 years, sweetened by aged rum syrup. Serving Suggestions: This Dessert rum is perfect neat or with a few cubes of ice. To add a twist, why not try adding a slice of pineapple. In a cocktail it lends it self to the sweeter style of drink. Rum Old fashions, Rum Manhattans and cocktails that call for sweet sherry as a modifier. Tasting Notes Big aromas of fruit cake, rumnraisin, cocoa, dried ginger, cinnamon and clove. Tropical fruits, bananas and toffee, banoffee pie. On the palate there is initial chocolatey notes, sweet toffee, fudge and tropical fruit flavours from the nose. The finish is long and sweet like sticky pudding. Lots of brown sugar, caramel, toffee and bananas with a touch of heat.

products.title: Ron Abuelo 7 Year Old - 70cl
products.description: Sweetened Rum Here we recommend rums that have been sweetened with the addition of aged sugar syrup, sweet wines or other sweetening agents to round off the rums flavour. Europe allows a maximum of 20grms of sugar per litre of alcohol to be added to rum. Ron Abuelo (literally 'Grandfather's rum in Spanish) is distilled from fermented molasses at the family owned Varela Hermanos distillery in Panama. This light bodied rum, distilled in a twin column still, is aged in American white oak ex-bourbon barrels for an average of seven years. The distillery is one of the few in the world that grow their own sugar cane. Serving Suggestions: This rum is perfect for high balls or long drinks as it is light & fruity and works well with tonic water, soda and ginger ale. If Mojitos are your style of drink then Abuelo 7 is the perfect base. Tasting Notes The 7 Años opens with a slight sweetness on the nose, followed by light aromas that conjure floral notes, dry grass and hints of dry sherry. Aromatic hints of mixed nuts and coconut announce a palate that starts with some heat and evolves into a blend of light fruit, caramel and vanilla. The medium sweet, long finish introduces some cedar, medium dry sherry and spice before tapering off into burnished leather.

products.title: Tamdhu 15 Year Old - 70cl
products.description: Scotch Whisky - Single Malt Despite its reputation as a somewhat traditional spirit, Scotch whisky offers incredible diversity of flavour, with single malts and blends ranging from elegant, floral expressions to rich, fruity and chocolatey drams. Speysides Tamdhu distillery is renowned for its rich, fruity and heavily-Sherried single malt whiskies, and this limited edition 15-year-old is no exception. Matured fully in ex-oloroso Sherry casks made from American and European oak, this is a rich and fruity whisky with a lasting finish. Serving Suggestions: Delicious enjoyed neat or in an Old Fashioned (stir 50ml with three dashes of Angostura bitters over ice, strain into a rocks glass and garnish with orange zest). Tasting Notes The nose is syrupy and sweet, but still fresh with apple blossom, orange zest and dried pineapple. On the palate the fruitiness bursts to life with more juicy pineapple, apricots and raspberry coulis, with a spiced yet creamy caramel and gingerbread sweetness.

products.title: Arran Machrie Moor - 70cl
products.description: Scotch Whisky - Single Malt Despite its reputation as a somewhat traditional spirit, Scotch whisky offers incredible diversity of flavour, with single malts and blends ranging from elegant, floral expressions to rich, fruity and chocolatey drams. Machrie Moor is a peated single malt produced on the Isle of Arran at Lochranza distillery, featuring all the fruitiness of the sites signature spirit with a puff of smoke. This sweet yet rugged whisky is named after the windswept peat bog on the west coast of the island where, legend has it, the warrior giant Fingal kept his pet dog. Serving Suggestions: Serve this one neat or over ice. Tasting Notes On the nose theres indulgent toffee, and tarte tatin, with chocolate-coated nuts and marshmallows toasted over a roaring fire. The fruits assume control on the palate, with juicy, tropical pineapple, green apples, pears and lemon candy, wrapped in a waft of dried grass and a lick of meaty smoke.

products.title: Nikka From the Barrel - 50cl
products.description: New World Whisky - Japan Blend Today there are hundreds of distilleries producing whisky in countries without a traditional heritage in the spirit, from England and Wales to Israel and Sweden. These new whisky makers are providing innovation and a whole new world of flavour. With its signature square bottle, Nikka From the Barrel is one of the most iconic Japanese whiskies around. A blend of grain whisky and single malts from the Miyagikyo and Yoichi distilleries that have been matured in a variety of casks, this is a powerhouse of a whisky bottled directly from the cask at close to cask strength. Serving Suggestions: Serve neat, on the rocks, or with soda water and ice in a refreshing Highball. Tasting Notes Its all vanilla, toffee and toasted oak on the nose with a delicate orange aura and black pepper spice. But this is a rich and powerful whisky, with plenty of dried fruit, citrus peel, cinnamon and cloves, with just a tiny hint of smoke toward the end. It finishes on bitter dark chocolate and a gentle Sherried smoke.

products.title: Rittenhouse Straight Rye 100 Proof - 70cl
products.description: American Whiskey - Rye The US is the spiritual heartland of Bourbon and rye whiskey, popularised around the world by classic cocktails from the Old Fashioned to the Manhattan. Distilled and matured at Heaven Hill distillery in Bernheim, Kentucky, Rittenhouse Straight Rye Whiskey has a storied heritage with roots in Philadelphia. This spicy, full-bodied rye is bottled-in-bond, which means it was produced at one distillery in a single season, matured for at least four years and bottled at 50% abv. Serving Suggestions: Rittenhouse is a solid benchmark whiskey for classic cocktails. Try it in an Old Fashioned, Manhattan or Boulevardier, or simply sip it neat. Tasting Notes Upfront its delicately honeyed with gentle aromas of toasted rye, caramel and sunflower seeds. The palate, however, is a different story  its bold, spicy and peppery, a heat that gradually subsides into toasted rye bread, cooked orchard fruits and runny honey with a hint of orange zest and cola cubes.

products.title: Martin Millers Westbourne Gin - 70cl
products.description: British Gin The UK is the motherland of gin, and remains its biggest producer. While gin is often believed to be a quintessentially English spirit, there many excellent gins made throughout the nation. Martin Millers Gin may be blended in Iceland, but it is distilled in the UK at the renowned Langley Distillery using two pot still distillations. Flavours of dried fruit, nutmeg, and masala spice linger pleasantly in the mouth.

products.title: Cotswolds 2015 Odyssey Barley - 70cl
products.description: New World Whisky - England Single Malt Today there are hundreds of distilleries producing whisky in countries without a traditional heritage in the spirit, from England and Wales to Israel and Sweden. These new whisky makers are providing innovation and a whole new world of flavour. The Cotswolds Distillery opened in 2014 on the outskirts of the eponymous English area of outstanding natural beauty. Surrounded by picturesque barley fields, the distillery produces a super fruity style of whisky, one thats gently kissed with subtle peat notes in its Peated Cask expression. Made using 100% local, floor-malted barley, this no-age-statement single malt is matured in ex-peated quarter casks and bottled at cask strength for a big flavour. Strong notes of tannin-rich malt, oils and dark sugar with lots of spice, caramelised Seville orange marmalade. Long and resinous, with dark red fruits and a hint of treacle

products.title: Makar Glasgow's Original Dry Gin - 70cl
products.description: British Gin The UK is the motherland of gin, and remains its biggest producer. While gin is often believed to be a quintessentially English spirit, there many excellent gins made throughout the nation. Makar is produced by The Glasgow Distillery Co, which opened in the Scottish city in 2014. The gin is distilled seven times in a copper pot still and contains seven botanicals that are typically found in London Dry gins, including cassia bark, coriander seed and angelica root. Makar may not play around with jazzy flavours, but it is a beautifully balanced, rounded product. One for those who like true, uncompromising, juniper-fuelled gin. Suggested serves: A simple G&T with Indian tonic, garnished with either dried juniper berries or a slice of ginger peel. Alternatively, swap the tonic for ginger ale to create an equally refreshing Gin Buck  just be sure to use heaps of ice and a good squeeze of lemon or lime juice. Tasting Notes Earthy juniper hits the nose first, followed by rose petals, thyme, fresh coriander and cut grass. Warm and dry palate with flavours of ginger, star anise, liquorice and pine complemented by a bright, clean menthol note. This gin has balance in abundance.

products.title: Chase Seville Marmalade - 70cl
products.description: Flavoured Gin While historically gin has been required to have a predominant taste of juniper, a cohort of products has emerged that champion other flavours. Some are full-strength spirits, while others are sweeter, lower-ABV liqueurs. This bright, zingy gin from UK distillery Chase is full of aromatic orange flavour. It is made by re-distilling potato-based Chase GB Gin with Seville orange peels, and then macerating the liquid with fresh Seville oranges for an unmistakably citrus flavour. Suggested serves: Perfect in a Spritz with white vermouth, orange bitters and tonic or soda. Also great in a Spanish-style G&T garnished with thick orange slices, or an orange-scented Negroni. Tasting Notes The nose presents bundles of sweet ripe orange, with supporting aromas of lemon peel and fresh coriander. On the palate, the orange is gentle and natural, balancing wonderfully with the juniper, which remains prominent. A dryness rolls across the palate, exposing additional flavours of coriander powder, mint and cinnamon.

products.title: Canaima Amazonian Gin - 70cl
products.description: World Gin Gin may be typically associated with the UK, but there are now many producers around the world who are putting their own spin on things by creating exciting expressions that reflect their local heritage and provenance. South American gin Canaima is produced by the same team behind Venezuelas excellent Diplomático rum. It is made using 10 sustainably sourced botanicals from the Amazon rainforest (including merey, túpiro and pijiguao), as well as one botanical from the distillerys region and eight traditional gin botanicals. Each botanical is macerated and re-distilled individually in small batches to extract maximum flavour. Suggested serves: The tart flavours of Canaima play well in Cobbler-style drinks. Try it with Sherry, lots of ice and a mix of tropical fruit slices. You easily whip up the Amazonian Gin signature serve using grapefruit soda, ice and a slice of fresh grapefruit. Tasting Notes Zippy aromas of grapefruit zest and passion fruit come first, followed by cooked rhubarb and cut grass. Herbal flavours evolve more on the palate, with notes of eucalyptus, basil and dry juniper. A pleasantly bitter finish rounds things off.

products.title: Never Never Distilling Co Triple Juniper - 50cl
products.description: World Gin Gin may be typically associated with the UK, but there are now many producers around the world who are putting their own spin on things by creating exciting expressions that reflect their local heritage and provenance. Australias Never Never Distilling Company, based in the south of the country, is known for its innovative production methods. Described as a modern classic, Never Never Triple Juniper Gin undergoes three distillation processes using copious amounts of juniper. First, juniper is steeped in alcohol for around 24 hours before the liquid, plus fresh juniper, is added to the pot still, with extra quantities of juniper added to the vapour basket. Suggested serves: Quinine-rich tonic waters should be used in G&Ts, and herbal garnishes work well. Never Never Triple Juniper also forms a great base for a Red Snapper, which is essentially a Bloody Mary made with gin instead of vodka. Tasting Notes A bold aroma of juicy juniper and zesty citrus, along with earthy cooked thyme. The palate opens with earthy juniper and black pepper, while a deliciously oily texture coats the palate. Hints of orange zest, honey and oak follow. Very rounded and integrated flavours from start to finish.

products.title: Four Pillars Spiced Negroni - 70cl
products.description: Modern Gin In this section, we highlight a selection of exceptional gins that use innovative production techniques or unusual ingredients (or both) to give the spirit a contemporary twist. From Australian distillery Four Pillars, based in Melbournes Yarra Valley, this gin has been specifically designed with the Negroni in mind. The aromatic quality and spiciness of the original Four Pillars has been hiked up in this expression, resulting in exalted flavour intensity and additional body. The distilling team also uses the West African spice grains of paradise and Indonesian cubeb to enhance the gins complexity. Suggested serves: A Negroni (obviously) made with equal parts Campari and sweet red vermouth. Try mixing with ice to dilute to your taste then pre-batching. The batched cocktail can be kept perfectly chilled in the fridge and doesnt need to be served with ice, making it ideal for dinner parties. Tasting Notes Surprisingly sweet, fruity nose with hints of candied orange peel and sour cherry. Rich spice slowly evolves on the palate, while the more delicate floral/herbal flavours of lavender and fresh oregano shine. The finish is peppery but with a refined herbaceous quality.

products.description: Modern Gin In this section, we highlight a selection of exceptional gins that use innovative production techniques or unusual ingredients (or both) to give the spirit a contemporary twist. Lime comes through strongly on the palate, followed by a complex flavour of spiced orange, tealeaves and piney juniper.

products.title: Fortaleza Blanco Still Strength - 70cl
products.description: Tequila Blanco Aged Tequila may command higher prices, but to many connoisseurs this remains the purest expression of Tequila, taken straight off the still or aged for up to two months. Also known as plata or silver, blanco Tequilas tell the story of their origins  in terms of the agave and the production methods used  with no oak to cover any faults. Fortaleza has only been operating since 2005, but the family behind it can trace its origins back to Don Cenobio Sauza, the father of Tequila, who opened his first distillery in 1873, established Sauza Tequila and was one of the pioneers of the drinks global reputation. The aim at Fortaleza is to make Tequila using the methods of a century ago  small brick oven, tahona, fermentation in wood and copper pots  and the result is a blanco Tequila of uncommon complexity and character, with the unmistakable agave character amplified in this cask strength bottling. Serving Suggestions: The exuberance of this distillate carries it far beyond traditional margarita and paloma territory to twists on any number of classic cocktails, including negronis and imaginative highballs. Tasting Notes Theres haystack aromas and white pepper up front, but this is all about the fruit, which is ripe, bright and sumptuous. Pineapple chunks and mango continue onto the opulent palate, where a whisper of earthiness and a pinch of anise carry through to an elegant, persistent finish. Classy.

products.description: Tequila Blanco Aged Tequila may command higher prices, but to many connoisseurs this remains the purest expression of Tequila, taken straight off the still or aged for up to two months. Also known as plata or silver, blanco Tequilas tell the story of their origins  in terms of the agave and the production methods used with no oak to cover any faults. The Orendain family have been making Tequila at their El Llano distillery in the heart of the town of Tequila since 1900, with the fifth generation now in charge. El Llano was rebuilt in 1978 and, eight years later, Arette was created, taking its name from a horse that won two showjumping gold medals at the London Olympics of 1948. Arette is made from 100% estate-grown valley agave, pressure-cooked to produce a pungent, but still elegant, style  and Arette Blanco is its purest expression. Serving Suggestions: A classic Tequila for classic Tequila cocktails  any number of riffs on the margarita theme, or a gutsy paloma. Forward and assertive, with lawnmower clippings and hedgerow florals. The gorgeous texture carries punchy black pepper and spice. Powerful and and mouthfilling, with a drying finish and that peppery character always to the fore.

products.title: Storywood Reposado Speyside - 70cl
products.description: Tequila Reposado Reposado means rested, and these Tequilas spend between two months and a year in oak. Factor in different cask types and you end up with a broad range of styles: some reposados have just the lightest lick of oak to add a little honey and vanilla creaminess to the punchy agave, while others have a more Bourbon-y toastiness to them. These are the all-rounders of the Tequila universe  great in cocktails but, at their best, worth sipping neat too. Most aged Tequila is put in regular ex-Bourbon casks, but the Storywood venture from Michael Ballantyne aims to unite his Scottish and Mexican heritage by using casks sourced from the Scotch whisky industry, creating a markedly different flavour profile as a result. This reposado uses punchy lowland agave matured for 10 years and spends seven months in a former Speyside single malt cask. Serving Suggestions: Live free, sip slow is the Storywood motto, but this is more of a mixer than a sipper. Theres enough weight and character here for some powerful stirred-down creations if you can find the right fruit match. Tasting Notes The first impression is of soft, rounded aromas of white pepper and creamy oak/vanilla. Theres restrained citrus and lifted mint. Nicely balanced. The palate shows clean, peppery agave and some earthy notes that hint at its lowland origin. Theres an intriguing herbal element (tarragon?) that becomes more vegetal, before a finish of honey, vanilla and curry spice.

products.title: Ocho Blanco - 50cl
products.description: Tequila Blanco Aged Tequila may command higher prices, but to many connoisseurs this remains the purest expression of Tequila, taken straight off the still or aged for up to two months. Also known as plata or silver, blanco Tequilas tell the story of their origins  in terms of the agave and the production methods used  with no oak to cover any faults. Few people have done as much for the global reputation of Tequila over recent decades as bar owner, restaurateur and Tequila ambassador Tomas Estes, including the creation of Ocho in partnership with Carlos Camarena, whose family have been making Tequila for almost a century. A 100% agave Tequila sourced entirely from Camarenas own fields, Ocho takes its name (eight in English) in part from the fact that this was the eighth recipe (muestra) presented to Estes by Camarena. The result is a consistently excellent range of characterful Tequilas. Serving Suggestions: The intensity and elegance of Ocho makes for a classic margarita with bags of agave character, but it works in a good range of mixed drinks and cocktails  think corpse revivers and sours. Tasting Notes Lightly vegetal and savoury (caraway) on the nose, with lifted notes of lime flower and citrus/green apple. The agave character asserts itself on the deft palate, alongside perfumed citrus flavours and freshly shelled garden peas. The savoury/caraway element returns on the finish, melting into earthiness  with an assertive white pepper note always there.

products.title: Tapatio Añejo - 50cl
products.description: Tequila Añejo Again, the clue is in the name, with añejo simply meaning aged. These Tequilas spend between one and three years in oak, which can translate into quite an impact on the relatively delicate flavours found in the raw agave spirit  especially if ex-American whiskey casks are used. This is a tightrope walk between agave and oak, with the finest examples allowing the former to shine while the latter contributes layers of complexity and secondary aromas. Sipping Tequilas for sure, but dont be shy of a little judicious mixing in high-end cocktails too. Were not quite done with the Camarenas. Don Felipe Camarena founded the La Alteña distillery in 1937 and started selling Tapatío three years later, with grandson Carlos now in charge of operations and making Tapatío alongside other Tequilas including Ocho and El Tesoro. After a long fermentation and traditional double distillation, this añejo spends 18 months in ex-Bourbon casks. Serving Suggestions: Characterful and smooth enough to sip, but capable of mixing with care  you dont want to lose the subtleties of the distillate here. Tasting Notes Shy and subtle on the nose, before perfumed elements of pot-pourri and Parma Violet emerge. The sweetshop theme continues, with pepper lurking in the background. The texture is wonderful, and the palate also brings baked orchard fruits with cinnamon and nutmeg. That spicy, peppery element is coming from both the agave and the oak  but its impossible to tell where one ends and the other begins.

products.title: Ocho Añejo - 70cl
products.description: Tequila Añejo Again, the clue is in the name, with añejo simply meaning aged. These Tequilas spend between one and three years in oak, which can translate into quite an impact on the relatively delicate flavours found in the raw agave spirit  especially if ex-American whiskey casks are used. Sipping Tequilas for sure, but dont be shy of a little judicious mixing in high-end cocktails too. If youre sceptical that Tequila, like wine, is capable of conveying terroir through aroma and taste, then this is a product that might just prove the case. Sourced from a single field and a single vintage, it spends a year in ex-American whiskey barrels. The pale liquid illustrates the restrained oak influence and the fact that no artificial colouring is added. Serving Suggestions: One to sip, savour and contemplate at some length. Tasting Notes The oak has a very light touch here, bringing creamy aromas of honey and agave nectar. Meanwhile, the distillate positively sings with lime and lifted floral notes. Theres a little vegetal character, but its very perfumed. The agave remains in charge on the palate, with the oak happy to sit back and bring some honey and an enticing texture. Slightly astringent on the finish, but a punchy, perfumed delight.

products.title: H by Hine VSOP - 70cl
products.description: VSOP/Similar Cognac While the lower-priced VS category accounts for the lions share of global Cognac volumes, the entry point to quality Cognac for most people remains VSOP, encompassing Cognacs aged for at least four years, and often far longer. Beyond the classification, some producers are now preferring to focus instead on provenance  in terms of sub-region or vineyard. The Jarnac-based house of Hine makes much of its wine connections, and this comes through in a range of Cognacs that prioritise aromatic floral and fruit flavours over oak influence. H by Hine is Hine letting its hair down, producing an exuberant and versatile VSOP that is at its best in a range of traditional and modern cocktails. Serving Suggestions: Youre spoilt for choice here, because this is as happy as a frozen shot as it is providing the base for a vibrantly fruity Sidecar, or just mixed over ice with ginger ale and a twist of lime. Tasting Notes Very lively and forward on the nose, with plush sweet fruit, vanilla, honey and ginger. The vibrancy continues on the palate, which is beautifully balanced, soft and silky with light spice and white pepper. Theres caramel on the finish with some peppery floral aromas. A delightful and accessible Cognac.

products.title: G4 Añejo - 70cl
products.description: Tequila Añejo Again, the clue is in the name, with añejo simply meaning aged. These Tequilas spend between one and three years in oak, which can translate into quite an impact on the relatively delicate flavours found in the raw agave spirit  especially if ex-American whiskey casks are used. This is a tightrope walk between agave and oak, with the finest examples allowing the former to shine while the latter contributes layers of complexity and secondary aromas. Sipping Tequilas for sure, but dont be shy of a little judicious mixing in high-end cocktails too. Tequila is a family affair for the Camarena family: while Carlos created Ocho, brother Felipe makes G4 at a Heath Robinson-esque distillery in Arandas, obsessing over quality details such as making sure the agave is baked from top and bottom to create even cooking. The emphasis is on the natural expression of agave character even when, as in this case, the distillate spends 18 months in ex-Bourbon barrels. Serving Suggestions: Mix with care  theres a lot going on here  or just sip and savour. Tasting Notes Theres a herbal, slightly vegetal edge to some bright lime and orange peel here, wrapped in a creamy, pepper-sprinkled texture. The vibrant fruit continues on the palate, with a hefty peppery kick and a drying, savoury finish with hints of sawmill. Charming on the nose, punchy on the palate, beautifully balanced and restrained.

products.title: Hattiers Egremont - 70cl
products.description: British Premium Rum Historically rums from the ex-British colonies were the most sought after in the world. Today we are seeing a rise in British companies importing rums from around the world to bring world class spirits to the British public under their own brand name. A combination of four exceptional aged rums softened with local Dartmoor water to creates an unadulterated premium rum that is accessible to everyone. With rums from Barbados, Dominican Republic, Guatemala and Panama this premium rum is unadulterated with no sugar added and finally blended and bottled in Devon. Serving Suggestions: Try this rum on the rocks or with your favourite ginger beer or ginger ale with the addition of a squeeze of fresh lime and dash of Angostura bitters. Also works well in light cocktails such as the Daiquiri, The Mojito and Rum Sours where the light fruity flavour of the rum combine well with the citrus. Tasting Notes Aromas of caramel, toffee, cacao, banana and apricot with a hint of light spice. A well-structured palate with cinnamon, nutmeg and black pepper spice, rich, toffee, coconut, cacao and apricot fruit. Dry lightly spicy finish with rich toffee, cacao and tasted oak.

products.title: BenRiach 21yo Classic Speyside - 70cl
products.description: Scotch Whisky - Single Malt Despite its reputation as a somewhat traditional spirit, Scotch whisky offers incredible diversity of flavour, with single malts and blends ranging from elegant, floral expressions to rich, fruity and chocolatey drams. BenRiach has matured this 21-year-old single malt in a combination of four different cask types: virgin American oak, ex-Bourbon barrels, PX-Sherry and red wine casks. The Speyside distillerys spirit plays beautifully with ex-wine casks, which amplify the fruity notes while adding layers of balanced complexity. This expression is part of the classic range of unpeated whiskies from the distillery, and is one of the first creations from master blender Dr Rachel Barrie when she joined the distillery in 2017. Serving Suggestions: Best enjoyed neat. Tasting Notes It starts out surprisingly fruity and vibrant with candied citrus peel, pears and orange zest with an undercurrent of creamy vanilla-spiked cookie dough. The cookies continue into the palate where an army of gingerbread men and a layer of delicate Sherry and red fruits rise to meet them. The finish is long and slightly dry, tainted with red wine and a creamy butteriness.

products.title: Benromach 15 Year Old - 70cl
products.description: Scotch Whisky - Single Malt Despite its reputation as a somewhat traditional spirit, Scotch whisky offers incredible diversity of flavour, with single malts and blends ranging from elegant, floral expressions to rich, fruity and chocolatey drams. This monster of a whisky, produced at Speysides Benromach distillery, is an intensely fruity, chocolatey and luscious single malt wrapped in a cloak of gentle smoke. Matured in a combination of first-fill Bourbon and Sherry casks, theres layer upon layer of forest fruits and dark chocolate  an absolute treat of a whisky. Serving Suggestions: Enjoy neat or mix into a Rob Roy. Stir 50ml Benromach 15 Year Old with 25ml sweet vermouth and one dash of Angostura bitters over ice, then strain into a chilled glass and garnish with a cherry and lemon twist. Tasting Notes Big and bold with bundles of dried fruits like figs, prunes and raisins with a generous helping of sticky toffee pudding, milk chocolate and a touch of leather. On the palate its bigger still, now with a decadent, cherry-chocolate laden Black Forest gateaux, sticky Jamaican ginger cake, crushed nuts and a puff of bonfire smoke. Beautifully balanced and indulgent.

products.description: Scotch Whisky - Blended Malt Despite its reputation as a somewhat traditional spirit, Scotch whisky offers incredible diversity of flavour, with single malts and blends ranging from elegant, floral expressions to rich, fruity and chocolatey drams. Sheep Dip has its roots in the town of Oldbury, Severn in the West Country of England, where it was first created by a publican as his in-house whisky during the 1970s. The recipe, a blend of 16 Highland and Speyside malt whiskies matured in first-fill barrels, has remained the same almost 50 years later. Serving Suggestions: A perfect base for cocktails of any kind, but works particularly well in an Old Fashioned or a Highball with lashings of ginger ale. Tasting Notes Sweet cereal on the nose with a warming waft of toffee popcorn and apple strudel covered in flaky, sugar-crusted pastry. It stays light and spritely in the mouth, with more apple pie, sugared almonds and orange zest with a chilli-spice kick.

products.title: Nc'Nean Organic Single Malt - 70cl
products.description: Scotch Whisky - Single Malt Despite its reputation as a somewhat traditional spirit, Scotch whisky offers incredible diversity of flavour, with single malts and blends ranging from elegant, floral expressions to rich, fruity and chocolatey drams. The first commercial release from sustainable distillery Ncnean is made using 100% organic malted barley and comes in a beautifully designed, recycled glass bottle. Furthermore, the distillery, located on the west coast of Scotland, is 100% powered by renewable energy. This signature release has been matured in a combination of American oak and red wine casks that develop Ncneans signature full-bodied sweetness. You could say this is a whisky that makes a big impression with a small footprint. Serving Suggestions: Ncneans signature serve is in a Highball, with two parts whisky to four parts soda water poured over plenty of ice and topped with a sprig of mint to garnish. Tasting Notes A light, sweet and fruity whisky with delicate aromas of lemon posset, desiccated coconut and creamy white chocolate. The fruit really emerges in the mouth though as peach, apricot and lemon zest with crème anglaise and generously buttered, toasted rye bread.

products.title: Chase GB Gin - 70cl
products.description: British Gin The UK is the motherland of gin, and remains its biggest producer. While gin is often believed to be a quintessentially English spirit, there many excellent gins made throughout the nation. An early pioneer of the British craft spirits movement, Herefordshire-based Chase is famed for its farm-to-bottle approach, using estate-grown potatoes to make its vodkas and gins. Chase GB Gin is its core gin expression, made by re-distilling Chase Original Vodka with 10 classic botanicals. It is fragrant and full-bodied  perfect for those who like their gins extra dry. Suggested serves: A classic G&T with heaps of ice and a slice of ginger. Also try mixing with cloudy apple juice and a squeeze of lime. Tasting Notes Lemon oil on the nose with notes of basil, a hint of cucumber and lots of fragrant juniper. The juniper becomes drier on the palate, with additional flavours of cinnamon bark, robust red chilli and orange peel. Finish is spicy and fresh.

products.title: Whistle Pigs 10 Year Old Rye Whisky - 70cl
products.description: American Whiskey - Rye The US is the spiritual heartland of Bourbon and rye whiskey, popularised around the world by classic cocktails from the Old Fashioned to the Manhattan. This 100% straight rye whiskey is distilled in Alberta, Canada where its initially aged in new American oak barrels. The whiskey is then transported south to the Whistlepig Farm in Vermont where it continues to age further, for up to 10 years, developing notes of warming rye spice and sweet caramel. Serving Suggestions: Delicious neat or in a Maple Old Fashioned with the sugar substituted for maple syrup  a true taste of Canada! Tasting Notes A warming aroma of fresh doughnuts and chocolate chip cookie dough, smothered in vanilla ice cream and a thick butterscotch sauce. On the palate its bready and peppery, with more sugar-dusted doughnuts filled with raspberry jam. Warm baking spices of clove and pepper build into the mid-palate as it ends on notes of liquorice and burnt caramels.

products.title: Berry Bros No 3 - 70cl
products.description: British Gin The UK is the motherland of gin, and remains its biggest producer. While gin is often believed to be a quintessentially English spirit, there many excellent gins made throughout the nation. This gin technically straddles the British and World categories since its recipe has been created by London wine and spirits merchant Berry Bros & Rudd, though the gin is distilled in Holland. Berry Bros enlisted the help of distilling and bartending experts to create this award-winning gin, which uses six classic botanicals. These botanicals are steeped in a 100-year-old copper pot still before distillation begins, resulting in a bold and uncluttered London Dry. Serving suggestions: Keep it classic with a Vesper  made with gin, vodka, quinquina and lemon  or a Martinez  made with gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino liqueur, Angostura bitters and orange. For a G&T, stick to Indian tonic water and garnish with grapefruit and fresh rosemary. Tasting Notes On the nose, piney juniper, mint and lemon oil come to the fore, followed by thyme and orange. A complex combination of citrus and spice run through the palate in equal measure, offering notes of grapefruit, angelica, cardamom and chilli. A spicy sensation lingers.

products.title: Hernö Gin - 50cl
products.description: World Gin Gin may be typically associated with the UK, but there are now many producers around the world who are putting their own spin on things by creating exciting expressions that reflect their local heritage and provenance. Produced in the small Swedish village of Dala, the core Hernö variant is a classic London Dry. Clean and precise, the gin is made from a base of wheat spirit with organic botanicals including Swedish lingonberries and Polish meadowsweet. The botanicals are macerated in the spirit for 18 hours before distilling, creating an intensely aromatic, full-bodied gin. Suggested serves: Hernö Dry is a great base for sour cocktails such as the Gin Fizz, made with gin, fresh lemon juice, sugar syrup and egg white. It also makes a cracking Hanky Panky, which contains gin, sweet red vermouth and Fernet-Branca. Tasting Notes Crisp aromas of eucalyptus, aniseed, vanilla and a touch of fresh brioche lead to a smooth palate of sweet licorice, cola bottles and green chilli. Flavours of white pepper and ginger linger on the finish.

products.title: Hernö Old Tom - 50cl
products.description: Other Style Gin Here we recommend some styles of gin that showcase the spirit in a different light. They include a sloe gin, an old Tom gin, a navy strength gin, and a cask-aged gin. Old Tom is a historical style of gin that has a sweeter taste profile than London Dry gin. It rose to prominence in the late 1800s when sweeter flavours were typically used to mask bad-quality spirit. Today, old Tom is delicious style for those looking for a gentler juniper flavour. From Swedish distillery Hernö, this old Tom gin is based on the same recipe as Hernö Dry Gin but with extra meadowsweet in the botanical mix and a touch of sugar added after dilution. Serving suggestions: A Tom Collins with lemon juice, sugar syrup and topped with soda. Hernö also recommends a Basil Smash, made with fresh basil leaves, lemon juice and sugar syrup. Tasting Notes Aroma is fresh, zesty and sweet  similar to that of old fashioned chocolate lime candies. A perfumed undercurrent of lavender, rose and fresh coriander follows. On the palate, the sweetness is subtle, adding a freshness to the prominent earthy character, creating flavours of oak spice, sweet basil and candied orange peel. Finish is bitter-sweet.

products.title: Elephant Gin - 50cl
products.description: Other Style Gin Here we recommend some styles of gin that showcase the spirit in a different light. They include a sloe gin, an old Tom gin, a navy strength gin, and a cask-aged gin. Navy strength gin is category with historical roots that must be bottled at a minimum of 57% ABV. The style gets its name from gins use by the Royal Navy in the 19th century, when sailors would test the strength of their spirits by attempting to light gunpowder. It was essential for spirits on-board to have a high strength so that if they spilt, gunpowder would remain explosive. Made in Germany using African botanicals, Elephant Strength Gin is an excellent example of the navy style. It contains double the quantity of botanicals used in the original Elephant Gin and shines a light on African buchu. Serving suggestions: Great in a classic G&T with Indian tonic and lots of lime. Also makes an excellent Gimlet, made with gin, lime juice and sugar syrup. Tasting Notes Rich aroma of squeezed lime and grapefruit, with stewed fruits, cooked biscuits and roasted hazelnuts. Wonderfully oily mouthfeel with flavours of citrus, earthy juniper, black pepper and sage. Finish is long and spicy.

products.title: Merlet Brothers Blend VSOP - 70cl
products.description: VSOP/Similar Cognac While the lower-priced VS category accounts for the lions share of global Cognac volumes, the entry point to quality Cognac for most people remains VSOP, encompassing Cognacs aged for at least four years, and often far longer. Beyond the classification, some producers are now preferring to focus instead on provenance  in terms of sub-region or vineyard. You might know Merlet best for the companys range of fruit liqueurs, but the family has been distilling eaux-de-vie in the Cognac region for well over 150 years. The Brothers in question here are Gilles Merlets sons Pierre and Luc, and this Cognac is billed as a new style for a new generation. That means highly approachable and mixable. Serving Suggestions: Were in classic Cognac cocktail territory here, particularly juleps, slings, sazeracs and old fashioneds. Or, for a more relaxed feel, simply over ice and/or tonic. Tasting Notes A surprisingly shy nose of delicate florals, fruit and something darker and spicier lurking in the background. By contrast, the palate is relatively big and boisterous, with sour cherry, cola cube and a drying finish. All about character rather than complexity.

products.title: Maxime Trijol Extra - 70cl
products.description: Extra/Vintage Cognac Cognacs hinterland beyond XO is one of great variation, but with the common thread of aged eaux-de-vie that have often spent many decades in cask. These are highly sought-after Cognacs for the top end of the market, characterised by that almost indefinable rancio character that only comes with great age. Vintages also inhabit this part of the market, but not always. These are Cognacs that run counter to the dominant local technique of blending, expressing the character of an individual harvest in a way that is reminiscent of fine wine. A family-run Cognac house for well over 150 years  most recently under Jean-Jacques Trijol and his two daughters  Maxime Trijol is unusual in carrying out the entire production process, from vineyards (Grande and Petite Champagne) to bottle. In a comprehensive portfolio of excellent Cognacs, Extra is a classically fine expression of Grande Champagne. Serving Suggestions: Just a good glass, and time. Tasting Notes Heady aromas of jasmine and violet leap out of the glass, alongside bright fruit and an umami hint of rancio. The texture is pure velvet, with ginger and drying oak filling out the mid-palate before the power builds with an irrepressible lift of forest floor rancio. Mouthfilling and intense, the gloriously endless finish brings dark chocolate and a spike of menthol.

products.title: Berry Bros Kings Ginger Liqueur - 50cl
products.description: Flavoured/Liqueur Gin While historically gin has been required to have a predominant taste of juniper, a cohort of products has emerged that champion other flavours. Some are full-strength spirits, while others are sweeter, lower-ABV liqueurs. First crafted by Berry Bros. & Rudd for King Edward VII in 1903, delightfully robust in flavour with a lovely golden colour. It starts with a sweetness on the palate and then is gently interrupted by the warming tingle of the fresh ginger, uplifting to a subtle taste of citrus lemon. Perfect to be savoured on its own, or mixed to offer a twist on some favourites such as a Negroni or a Mule, or even as an addition to a warming Mulled Cider. Now made in the UK.

products.title: Ilegal Joven - 70cl
products.description: Mezcal Often characterised as the lawless cousin of Tequila, mezcal is in fact a legally regulated spirit found in various parts of Mexico, but most famously in the southern state of Oaxaca. It is made using various types of agave  while Tequila is a monoculture of blue agave, mezcal uses dozens of sub-species  and a highly artisanal production method. Traditionally, mezcal agave is baked in underground earth ovens, which imparts the distinctive aromas for which it is famed. But techniques  and the flavours they impart  vary enormously among the multiplicity of small mezcal producers. Like Tequila, mezcal can be unaged (joven or young), or aged in wood for months or sometimes years. Most often consumed neat in Mexico, mezcal is now finding a place on many cocktail lists across the US and Europe. What started out as a way for company founder John Rexer to supply his bar in Antigua Guatemala with mezcal (not always officially, as the name suggests) is now a thriving business in which rum giant Bacardi owns a stake. Respectability hasnt changed the authentic core of Ilegal, however, which manages to convey the essential character of mezcal in a supremely accessible way. Serving Suggestions: This is a great introduction to mezcal, so neat is the way to go  but it makes for an intriguing comparison with a traditional Tequila margarita, where that earthy smoke really cuts through. Tasting Notes Highly perfumed nose of smouldering greenwood, spice and bonfire embers. Very earthy, but still refined, with warm citrus  ripe orange skin in particular. The palate brings more of that savoury, earthy smoke, but theres enough restraint to allow the perfumed fruit to return. The finish is redolent of a neglected bonfire smouldering in a rain shower. Nicely balanced between smoothness and spiky character.

What started out as a way for company founder John Rexer to supply his bar in Antigua Guatemala with mezcal (not always officially, as the name suggests) is now a thriving business in which rum giant Bacardi owns a stake. Respectability hasnt changed the authentic core of Ilegal, however, which manages to convey the essential character of mezcal in a supremely accessible way.

Serving Suggestions: This is a great introduction to mezcal, so neat is the way to go  but it makes for an intriguing comparison with a traditional Tequila margarita, where that earthy smoke really cuts through.

Tasting Notes

Highly perfumed nose of smouldering greenwood, spice and bonfire embers. Very earthy, but still refined, with warm citrus  ripe orange skin in particular. The palate brings more of that savoury, earthy smoke, but theres enough restraint to allow the perfumed fruit to return. The finish is redolent of a neglected bonfire smouldering in a rain shower. Nicely balanced between smoothness and spiky character.

products.title: Four Pillars Bloody Shiraz -70cl
products.description: Flavoured Gin While historically gin has been required to have a predominant taste of juniper, a cohort of products has emerged that champion other flavours. Some are full-strength spirits, while others are sweeter, lower-ABV liqueurs. Not your typical flavoured gin, Four Pillars Bloody Shiraz is made by steeping cool climate Shiraz grapes from the Yarra Valley in the distillerys Rare Dry expression for eight weeks. On the palate, a sweet wine taste mixed with fresh strawberry and cooked apple is prominent, but a delicate floral note of juniper permeates. A beautifully smooth finish extends the juniper flavour.

products.title: Kyrö Dark Gin - 50cl
products.description: Other Style Gin Here we recommend some styles of gin that showcase the spirit in a different light. They include a sloe gin, an old Tom gin, a navy strength gin, and a cask-aged gin. Cask-aged gin has been growing in popularity in recent years, giving drinkers a taste of complex wood spice. Often, cask-aged gins are matured for a number of months in oak, but other types of woods are also used. Such gins can be sipped on their own or used in a mixed drink. Kyrös gin takes on a golden colour and rich honeyed flavour in this cask-aged expression. To create Kyrö Dark Gin, the Finnish distilling team matures their wholegrain rye-based gin in American oak casks for three to 12 months. Serving suggestions: Trying sipping neat with ice  you can always add a little sugar syrup to sweeten things up. You could also give your old fashioned a botanical twist by swapping Bourbon for Kyrö Dark Gin. Tasting Notes Sweet cola bottles and cumin on the nose with additional aromas of licorice, manuka honey and chamomile. The candied cola bottle aroma carries through to the palate, which also presents black pepper, vanilla and fresh red chilli with a fresh herbal element.

products.description: Modern Gin In this section, we highlight a selection of exceptional gins that use innovative production techniques or unusual ingredients (or both) to give the spirit a contemporary twist. Suggested serves: A Kyrö G&T is best garnished with cranberries and fresh rosemary. You could also swap vodka for Kyrö Gin to make a gin-based twist on the cranberry-flavoured Cosmopolitan. The sweetness is balanced by citrus and soft warm allspice.

products.title: Chamarel VSOP - 70cl
products.description: Sugarcane Juice Rum Most Rums are made from molasses, a by-product of making sugar. But in this section, we highlight a selection of exceptional Rums made from fresh sugarcane juice. Less than 5% of the worlds production of rum is made this way and the process yields a dramatically different product. La Rhumerie de Chamarel is located on the African island of Mauritius, situated several hundred miles east of Madagascar in the Indian Ocean. The distillery cultivates its own sugarcane thus creating estate rums. The freshly harvested sugarcane is transferred to the distillery within 4 hours of being cut to preserve its freshness and aromas. This Pure Cane Rum is a blend Column Still and pot still rums. Each Rum is aged separately for 4 to 6 years in American Oak Barrels & French Oak Barrels. Serving Suggestions: Chamarel VSOP is perfect neat, on the rocks with a twist of orange peel or with your favourite mixer. In an Old-Fashioned cocktail, the rum truly shines, especially in a Treacle style of cocktail adding fresh apple juice to a traditional rum old fashion cocktail. Tasting Notes Initial aromas of light vanilla pods, toffee, orange oils, lemon peels and oak. The taste starts with a complex harmony of spices and dried fruits, then notes of vanilla, smooth oak, orange, pepper and clove. The finish is medium and dry, with tropical fruits, white pepper, dried oak with a touch of warm liquorice and aniseed.

products.description: Sweetened Rum Here we recommend rums that have been sweetened with the addition of aged sugar syrup, sweet wines or other sweetening agents to round off the rums flavour. A classic triple-distilled Irish single malt from Walsh Whiskeys The Irishman range. This no-age-statement whisky, sourced from an unnamed distillery and crafted in small batches of just 6,000 bottles, is matured in a combination of ex-oloroso Sherry and Bourbon casks for a fruity, chocolatey and rich depth of flavour.

Serving Suggestions: Serve with 20ml of strawberry puree and top with Champagne or Prosecco for a sparkling, celebratory drink.

Tasting Notes

An elegantly floral yet fruity and inviting nose with warming aromas of chocolate, caramel and crunchy roasted almonds alongside ripe peach and dried fruits. As the silky texture glides across the tongue it becomes sweeter, with notes of honeycomb, juicy sultanas and an exotic fruitiness. Still, its that creamy milk chocolate and toasted oak that leave a long and lasting impression.

products.title: Malfy Con Limone - 70cl
products.description: Flavoured Gin While historically gin has been required to have a predominant taste of juniper, a cohort of products has emerged that champion other flavours. Some are full-strength spirits, while others are sweeter, lower-ABV liqueurs. A fun expression for those with a bit of a sweet tooth, Malfy Con Limone brings a touch of Italian sunshine to wherever you are. The gin is made in Moncalieri, Italy, using Italian lemons  some of which are of the famed Amalfi variety as well as Italian juniper from Tuscany. Suggested serves: Enjoy as a Spritz during aperitivo hour by mixing with soda, topping with Prosecco and garnishing with blueberries, lemon and basil. Alternatively, go full throttle by mixing with homemade lemonade. Tasting Notes Sweet lemon sherbet nose with lime candies and lavender. Piney juniper, coriander seed and zesty lemon play together harmoniously on the palate. Nice viscous mouthfeel and a sweet finish that is clean rather than cloying.

products.title: Thomas Dakin - 70cl
products.description: British Gin The UK is the motherland of gin, and remains its biggest producer. While gin is often believed to be a quintessentially English spirit, there many excellent gins made throughout the nation. Thomas Dakin is a juniper-led London Dry that celebrates traditional gin making, using 11 botanical including English coriander and horseradish. The gin is named after an early pioneer of quality English gin, who began distilling in the mid-1700s. Thomas Dakin is currently made by G&J Distillers in Warrington, close to where Dakin distilled his original gin, though plans are underway to move production to a new craft distillery in Manchester. Suggested serves: Makes a fantastic Negroni (with sweet red vermouth, Campari and orange peel). The brand also recommends a take on the Cosmopolitan, swapping vodka for Thomas Dakin gin. Tasting Notes Initial aromas of dried orange peel and cumin give way to fresh grapefruit and rosemary. The gins use of horseradish gives the palate a wonderful dryness and a rich, savoury flavour. A light spice coats the mouth, while delicate flavours of fresh coriander and sweet orange slowly evolve and linger on the finish.

products.title: Ki No Bi Kyoto Dry Gin - 70cl
products.description: World Gin Gin may be typically associated with the UK, but there are now many producers around the world who are putting their own spin on things by creating exciting expressions that reflect their local heritage and provenance. With a name that translates as The Beauty of the Seasons, Ki No Bi is a distinctly Japanese gin. Made in a small distillery in the ancient city of Kyoto, the gin uses a rice spirit as its base, which is flavoured with Japanese botanicals yellow yuzu, hinoki wood chips, bamboo, gyokuro tea and green sansh? berries, in addition to some more traditional gin botanicals. The botanicals are grouped into six flavour camps, which are individually distilled before being expertly blended. Suggested serves: Wonderful in a dry Martini with a citrus twist. Swap the vermouth for sake to enjoy a fittingly Japanese Martini-style serve. The zesty character of Ki No Bi also perfectly suits a Clover Club cocktail, made with gin, vermouth, raspberry syrup, lemon juice and egg white. Tasting Notes A prominent citrus aroma of tangy yuzu  a bit like a lemon-lime-grapefruit hybrid  comes to the fore, with a background of smashed basil and white pepper. Bold flavours of lime, clove, spiced orange and rich oak follow, leaving a warm, tingling finish.

products.title: Sipsmith Chili  & Lime - 70cl
products.description: Flavoured Gin While historically gin has been required to have a predominant taste of juniper, a cohort of products has emerged that champion other flavours. Some are full-strength spirits, while others are sweeter, lower-ABV liqueurs. Made by London distiller Sipsmith, this exotic gin is flavoured with seven varieties of chilli from around the world  including Scotch bonnet, Carolina Reaper and Guajillo varieties  and Asian limes. Produced in small batches, Sipsmith Chilli & Lime is a delicious savoury gin, ideal for those looking for something a bit different. Suggested serves: Ideal replacement for vodka in a Bloody Mary. Also try as a substitute for Tequila and rum in twists on the classic Margarita and Mojito cocktails. Tasting Notes The nose is both earthy and buttery, like freshly baked buttered bread, with additional notes of dark chocolate, oak spice and lime zest. The palate is quite bitter, with flavours warm chilli, dry juniper and cooked orange. Earthy flavours linger on the finish, offset with a surprising sweetness.

products.title: Edinburgh Rhubarb Ginger Liqueur - 50cl
products.description: Liqueur While historically gin has been required to have a predominant taste of juniper, a cohort of products has emerged that champion other flavours. Some are full-strength spirits, while others are sweeter, lower-ABV liqueurs. The one and only gin-based liqueur in our selection, this product from Edinburgh Gin Distillery packs heaps of nostalgic flavours that, despite their sweetness, never overwhelm or cloy. To make the expression, Edinburgh Gin is infused with fresh rhubarb and ginger, which are steeped in the spirit for four weeks. Other botanicals include mulberry, orange and lemongrass. Suggested serves: Goes perfectly in a Bramble, which also consists of full-strength gin, blackberry liqueur and lemon. Its also delicious mixed with ginger beer, elderflower tonic, or lemonade, or simply sipped on its own over ice. Tasting Notes One sniff of this liqueur will instantly evoke the thrill of opening paper bag of old-fashioned rhubarb and custard sweets  its sweet, juicy, slightly sour, and very moreish. On the palate, a gentle sweetness carries flavours of cherry, lemonade and lavender, with a subtle kick of warm ginger rounding off the experience.
